title: Per-request KPI ingest sidecar for inference telemetry aggregation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: We need a lightweight ingest sidecar that co-locates with inference workers and normalizes per-request telemetry into a compact, Prometheus-friendly envelope. Current ingestion flows emit highly cardinal per-request labels and inconsistent KPI derivations (latency percentiles, token counts, cold-start flags) which lead to high storage cost and noisy SLIs. This sidecar will: 1) collect OTLP spans/metrics and structured request metadata from the local worker process, 2) synthesize canonical inference KPIs (request_latency_ms_p50/p95/p99, request_tokens_generated, kv_cache_hit_rate, cold_start_count, model_variant), 3) perform label cardinality reduction via hashing and bucketing for user-facing labels (e.g., prompt_template_id -> prompt_template_bucket), 4) apply deterministic sampling weight and emit aggregated metrics to the central metrics pipeline (Prometheus pushgateway / OTLP exporter) and 5) tag events for downstream trace correlation.
acceptance_criteria: Sidecar deployed as a Docker sidecar on perf staging cluster and receives OTLP metrics from a local worker process
Canonical KPIs emitted with stable metric names and label set; p50/p95/p99 computed using HDR histograms and exposed as Prometheus summaries or exemplars for correlation

Cardinality reduction algorithm limits unique label combinations to <10k per cluster per hour while preserving top-20 heavy hitters; sampled weight metadata is attached for accurate global aggregation
End-to-end tests: synthetic workload produces expected KPI deltas and Grafana dashboard shows coherent per-model SLO derivations compared to baseline
tech_notes: Architecture: sidecar reads local OTLP over gRPC and a small UNIX socket ingestion API used by the worker to submit request-scoped metadata; transforms are applied in-memory and periodically flushed
Aggregation: use HDR histogram for latency windows and burst-aware flush intervals (100ms flush, 1s burst coalescing). Expose exemplars to trace IDs for sampling-based latency attribution

Label strategy: canonical labels include service, model_family, model_variant, region, and prompt_template_bucket; freeform user labels are hashed and bucketed into 64 bins to avoid cardinality explosion
Export: primary export via OTLP/HTTP to telemetry-gateway with fallback to Prometheus pushgateway for legacy consumers. Use delta-encoding for counters when exporting to Prometheus to avoid resets
Configuration: feature flags for sampling_ratio (0.01-1.0), bucket_count, and histogram_buckets available via ConfigMap or environment variables
Resource budget: sidecar target memory <120MB and single-threaded CPU; implement backpressure (drop non-critical metrics) when worker load >90%
risks: Incorrect hashing/bucketing could hide critical customer-specific SLO regressions; mitigate via canary on low-traffic customers and top-k passthrough
Sidecar failure modes can affect local worker stability; run with process-level cgroup limits and graceful degradation (worker continues serving without sidecar if crash)
Potential incompatibility with existing Prometheus scrape semantics; ensure exporters adhere to Prometheus conventions and include monotonic counters where required
